transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because people keep acting like this foreclosure is just regular paperwork, like, “Oh, missed payments, sign this, call that number,” but that’s not what’s happening. The bank and the loan servicer have been working together, and I’m pretty sure people at my job know about it too—like the way they stop talking when I walk into the break room, and my supervisor suddenly asking weird questions about my schedule.

It’s been going on for almost two years, and they keep showing me papers like that’s supposed to make me ignore what I’ve been seeing. I know it sounds like a lot, but I’m not stupid. I’ve worked retail long enough to know when people are coordinating behind your back.
Do you believe that people are working together against you in a coordinated way, such as the bank, the loan servicer, and your coworkers all being involved in a plan directed at you?

Yes. I mean, that’s exactly what I’m trying to say, but everyone keeps making it sound like I’m being dramatic or not understanding forms. It’s not just “missed payments” and “paperwork.” The bank and the loan servicer, they’re not separate the way they pretend to be, and then at work people start acting strange too, like they already know something before I’ve even said anything.

And it’s been almost two years of this, so it’s not like I just woke up one day and decided that. I’ve seen how they move things around, how the timing lines up. They can hand me all the papers they want, but that doesn’t erase what I’ve been seeing.
Do you feel like these people are not only working against you but also trying to send you hidden messages or test your awareness through their actions?

I don’t know if I’d call them “messages,” exactly, but yes, it feels like they’re doing things on purpose to see if I notice. Like everyone keeps saying it’s just foreclosure paperwork, missed payments, forms, all that, but I’m telling you, the bank and the loan servicer have been working together, and then people at my job start acting like they’re in on it too.

And I’ve been a supervisor in retail, so I know how people act when they’re trying to keep something quiet. It’s the little pauses, the timing, the way something happens right after I ask a question. They can put a stack of papers in front of me and act like that explains everything, but it doesn’t change what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. They’re trying to push me out of my house, and they want me to second-guess myself.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others don't seem to notice, like voices, visions, or other unusual perceptions?

I mean… I don’t think I hear voices, if that’s what you mean. Not like someone talking when nobody’s there. And I’m not seeing, like, things floating around or anything.

It’s more that I notice patterns other people act like they don’t notice. Like at work, when somebody stops mid-sentence, or the timing of calls and papers and questions feels too lined up. But that’s not a “vision,” you know? That’s just paying attention. So… no, not really, not in the way you’re asking.
Do you ever feel like people are plotting against you or trying to harm you when there's no clear reason for it?

Yes, I do. I mean, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, like I didn’t fill out the right thing or I’m confused. But that’s not what this is.

The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job… they’ve been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And I know how that sounds when I say it out loud, but I’ve been watching it for almost two years. The timing, the way people react, the way things happen right after I ask questions—it’s not random.

And it’s like, at work, I’m supposed to be focused on schedules and customers and making sure the cashiers aren’t calling out again, but then someone makes a comment or gets quiet in a way that connects back to the house situation. So no, there may not be some big obvious reason they’ll admit to, but that doesn’t mean there isn’t a reason. The papers they keep showing me don’t change what I’ve seen.
Do you feel that certain events, comments, or actions happening around you have special meaning or are directed at you personally, even if others don’t see it that way?

Yes. That’s exactly what I mean. Certain comments or things that happen, they’re not just random to me. People keep saying, “It’s just foreclosure paperwork,” or “You missed payments,” like I’m supposed to accept that and stop asking questions. But I know the bank and the loan servicer have been working together, and somehow people at my job are tied into it too.

Like, I’ll be at work trying to deal with a return or fix a schedule because someone called out again, and then somebody says something in this careful way, or gets quiet right when I walk by, and it connects back to the house. I notice it. I’ve been seeing this for almost two years now.

So yes, I think some of it is directed at me personally. They can keep showing me papers, but that doesn’t change what’s actually been happening.
Do you feel that your understanding of what’s happening with the bank, the loan servicer, and your coworkers is correct, even if others present evidence or explanations that contradict it?

Yes. I mean… yes, I do think I’m right about it. That’s the thing people keep missing. They bring out these papers and say, “See, it’s just missed payments,” or “This is how foreclosure works,” like if they put enough forms in front of me I’m supposed to ignore everything else.

But I’ve been living with this for almost two years. I notice when the bank says one thing and then the loan servicer does something else, and then at work somebody makes some little comment—like not even directly, but enough that you know they know something. And then I’m supposed to just go back to covering breaks and dealing with customers wanting to return used stuff with no receipt, like nothing is happening.

So, yes, even if other people call it evidence or explanations, it doesn’t change what I’ve seen. The bank, the servicer, and people at my job have been working together to push me out of my house. I know that.

Even when people have shown you documents or explained things differently, do you still feel certain that your understanding of the situation is the true one and that others are trying to mislead you?

Yes. I mean, that’s what I keep trying to say. They can show me documents all day, but papers can be made to look clean, you know? At work we have paperwork for everything too—returns, schedules, write-ups—and half the time it doesn’t tell the real story of what happened on the floor.

So when they say it’s just missed payments or regular foreclosure steps, I don’t buy that. Not after almost two years of watching the bank say one thing, the loan servicer do another, and then people at my job acting like they know more than they should. It’s all connected. They’re trying to make me look like I’m misunderstanding it, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Have you ever believed in things that most people would find extremely strange or implausible, even if you can’t prove them with regular evidence?

I don’t know if I’d call it “extremely strange.” Other people act like it’s strange because they don’t want to look at what’s right in front of them. I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but it isn’t just that.

The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I know how it sounds, but when you’ve watched it happen for almost two years—little comments, timing, the way people suddenly know things they shouldn’t—it stops being a coincidence.

And regular evidence… I mean, papers can say anything. At my store, half the time the paperwork doesn’t match what actually happened with a customer or an employee, but management still waves it around like it proves something. So no, I can’t prove it the way they want me to, but that doesn’t mean I’m wrong.

Have you ever had similar kinds of beliefs about other situations in your life, where you felt people were working against you or that events had special meaning, even if they didn’t seem connected to the foreclosure or your job?

I mean… I don’t know about “other situations.” People keep trying to make it sound like this is some pattern with me, like I’m always looking for hidden meanings in everything, but that’s not what I’m saying.

This is about the house. The foreclosure. The bank saying it’s just paperwork and missed payments, the loan servicer acting like they’re just following procedure, and then people at my job somehow knowing things or making comments at the exact wrong time. That’s what I keep coming back to, because that’s what’s been happening for almost two years.

And it’s funny, because at work, customers will swear they didn’t use something when you can literally see it’s been used, and management still wants us to smile and pretend the receipt explains everything. So when people wave papers at me like that proves I’m wrong, I just… no. I know what I’ve been seeing. The bank, the servicer, and even people at work have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. That’s the situation I’m talking about.
